title: Verify then Steer: Progress Hallucination-Aware Recovery for Continuous Vision-and-Language Navigation
abstract: arXiv:2611.32400v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an agent to follow language instructions to reach a target in an unseen 3D environment. However, existing methods still struggle to recover from route deviations at test time. We investigate this limitation through the lens of instruction progress, and trace it to a phenomenon we term progress hallucination: agents misinterpret off-route observations as evidence of task progress, causing their internal instruction progress to advance beyond the actual task stage and hindering recovery based on earlier sub-instructions. To address this failure mode, we propose PHAR (Progress Hallucination-Aware Recovery), a test-time recovery framework following a verify-then-steer paradigm. The verifier examines residual-stream representations of the Vision-Language Model (VLM) to identify mismatch of cross-modal evidence along the trajectories, and uses split conformal calibration to control false alarms.

translated_title: 先验证再引导：面向连续视觉-语言导航的进度幻觉感知恢复
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言导航（VLN）要求智能体遵循语言指令，在未见过的3D环境中到达目标位置。然而，现有方法在测试时仍然难以从路线偏离中恢复。我们通过指令进度的视角研究这一局限，并将其追溯至我们称之为“进度幻觉”的现象：智能体将偏离路线的观察错误地解读为任务进展的证据，导致其内部的指令进度超前于实际任务阶段，从而阻碍了基于较早子指令的恢复。为了解决这一失败模式，我们提出了PHAR（进度幻觉感知恢复），这是一个遵循“先验证后引导”范式的测试时恢复框架。验证器检查视觉-语言模型（VLM）的残差流表示，以识别轨迹中跨模态证据的不匹配，并使用分裂保形校准来控制误报。
tldr: 提出PHAR测试时恢复框架，通过检测视觉-语言模型残差流表示中的跨模态证据不匹配来识别“进度幻觉”现象，使导航智能体能够从路线偏离中有效恢复。
en_tdlr: Proposes PHAR, a test-time recovery framework that detects "progress hallucination" by identifying cross-modal evidence mismatch in VLM residual-stream representations, enabling VLN agents to recover from route deviations.
